title: How Corner Is a Corner Case? Percentile Control for Highway Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: A requested risk percentile p, i.e. the position of the scenario's minimum PET in the history-conditioned natural distribution of future risk; a learned reference maps p to a physical PET target.

control_mechanism.value: Diffusion model conditioned on p, the physical risk target and a CDF descriptor, plus sampling-time risk guidance steering outputs to the target; road and separation constraints act in the same sampling path.

base_model.value: Joint multi-agent diffusion model with masked actor attention; reference risk distribution from temporal Transformers over absolute and ego-relative histories, trained with CRPS.

datasets.value: highD highway drone dataset; 11,649 natural clips used for reference evaluation.

metrics.value: Percentile MAE, fine-control rate within 0.05 tolerance, PET-target MAE, footprint overlap, road compliance; kinematic realism via Wasserstein-1 on speed and acceleration, harsh braking and implausible acceleration rates.

controllability_evidence.value: 1,422 of 1,440 requests realized within 0.05 percentile tolerance (98.75%), mean percentile error 0.00673, PET-target error 0.00991 seconds. Ablation: guidance alone realizes most requests; conditioning alone realizes few.

stated_limitations.value: Only highway scenarios on highD and one surrogate (PET); percentile is only as accurate as its reference; each model trained once; planner test uses non-reactive surrounding vehicles.

notes: Could also be labelled reward/risk conditioning; ablation indicates guidance supplies most precision, so inference-time guidance chosen. Kinematic realism of full method is mixed in Table 4 (harsh braking 0.18%, implausible 0.09%).
